fever._note: GDD 8.3. Rates sit at the slow end of the sanctioned ranges (distance 0.03~0.07, coin 0.8~1.6): at the defaults the gauge filled in ~45s, under the 50~70s target, because a coin-heavy line charges far faster than the distance-only sanity check in 8.3 assumes. ~68s now. durationSec 5.0 -> 7.5 (GDD 8.3 revision, user request): five seconds ended before the payoff registered. Tune from measured per-minute distance/coins/near-miss, never by hardcoding elsewhere. | 2026-08-21: durationSec 7.5 -> 9.5 (user request, balance pass).

items._note: Item table (user spec 2026-08-13). placement: risk = near a hazard so the pickup costs a manoeuvre; safe = in a clear stretch; neutral = anywhere. Weights give bigcoin/magnet/bolt 'medium' frequency and shield 'low'. | 2026-08-21: boltFeverChargePct 30 -> 100 (user request). The lightning now fills the gauge outright and fever fires on pickup, so it is a guaranteed payoff rather than a partial top-up. | 2026-08-21: heart added at weight 2 — rarer than the three medium pickups but ahead of the shield, since it is the only way to undo damage. | 2026-08-21: magnetDurationSec 6.0 -> 7.0 (user request, balance pass). | 2026-08-21: shield removed (user call). Hearts already absorb a hit, so a stackable one-hit shield was the same mechanic twice; its weight goes to the remaining pickups.

hp._note: GDD v6.0 §6 (STEP 2). One hit costs one heart and grants invulnerability so a single obstacle cannot eat the whole bar on consecutive frames. A pit costs a heart and returns her to solid ground before it rather than ending the run. §18 leaves these open until play-testing; these are the first pass, not a balanced answer. | 2026-08-21: heart pickup added (user request). max stays the stage-start value; maxCap is the ceiling a pickup can raise it to, and the item stops spawning at the cap. | 2026-08-21: invulnerableMs 1400 -> 520. At 1400 the mercy window covered 472px at pace — wider than the 390px screen — so a second, genuinely separate obstacle was absorbed for free. The player would take two hits, expect one heart left, then survive a pit and read it as being revived (user report). The window only needs to outlast one obstacle's own overlap, which is a few frames; 520ms covers ~175px, about four obstacle widths.

score._note: GDD v6.0 §7 first pass. §18 leaves the formula open until balance testing, so these are a starting shape, not an answer. Near miss is worth five coins because it costs a deliberate risk; a surviving heart is worth twenty because HP is the resource the whole stage is played against. clearBonus dominates a short stage on purpose — finishing is the point, and the rest is how well. | 2026-08-21: nearMissBandPx 22 -> 70. Measured live, she clears a hazard by 90-104px on a normal jump — her single-jump apex is 126.8px against obstacles 24 to 36 tall — so a 22px band could never be entered and near misses effectively never fired (user report). 70 sits under the 90px floor of an ordinary pass, so an ordinary jump still earns nothing; it pays for a late, low pass where she is already descending over the hazard. | 2026-08-21: band 70 -> 95 (user asked for more of them). Measured clearances on a normal jump run 50-104px, so 95 catches most passes; the call is graded by how close she actually came, so a loose pass reads Good! and only a tight one reads Perfect!. | 2026-08-21: band 95 -> 58. At 95 an ordinary jump cleared by 90-104px and still landed inside it, so almost every hazard paid out and the call stopped meaning anything (user report). 58 sits below that ordinary clearance, so a normal jump earns nothing and only a deliberately late, low pass does. | 2026-08-31: band 58 -> 65 (TASK-NEARMISS-FIX.md #3 — gap now measured off the arcade body, not the sprite AABB, so the same jump reads a bigger gap than before). Measured live: player body bottom sits 3px above the sprite's own bottom edge; a ground obstacle's body top sits 3-7px below its sprite top depending on skin (smallRock/stump 3px, the largeRock person-shaped variant 7px, its display 56x73 vs body 32x66). A normal jump's body-based gap is therefore roughly 6-10px larger than the sprite-based 50-104px this band was tuned against, so the boundary moves by the same rough amount to keep sitting under ordinary clearance rather than inside it. Still a starting shape — the original 50-104px range itself was never re-measured body-first end to end, only reasoned from these per-hazard shift constants.
